chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Bint Ilyas, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not proper for a man to give butter as a loan in exchange for oil, nor oil as a loan in exchange for butter.'

key_terms.إِسْلَافُ: Giving a loan of a specific commodity to be repaid with another
key_terms.السَّمْنِ: Butter (specifically clarified butter used in trade)
key_terms.بِالزَّيْتِ: With oil (specifically olive oil or similar)
key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: It is not proper / It is not permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging butter for oil in a loan transaction in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) within the chapter on selling guaranteed goods, specifically addressing the *qard* (loan) of fungible commodities. The prohibition against exchanging butter for oil or vice versa prevents *riba al-fadl* (excess usury) by ensuring equivalence in kind and quality, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence regarding commodity loans. This highlights the Imam’s emphasis on precision in trade to avoid hidden inequalities that might arise from differing market values or qualities of similar goods.
